hook.en: Two mobile companies in Mysuru fight for the same customers. Whatever one gains, the other loses. Game *theory*, founded by John von Neumann, tells each one the best strategy against a clever opponent.

title.en: Define a two-person zero-sum game and the payoff matrix
Find the saddle point and the value of the game

say.en: Two mobile companies in Mysuru fight for the same customers. Whatever one gains, the other loses. Game theory, founded by John von Neumann, tells each one the best strategy against a clever opponent. In this lesson: Define a two-person zero-sum game and the payoff matrix.
Apply the maximin-minimax principle.
Find the saddle point and the value of the game.

body.en: A game is a competitive situation between players with conflicting interests. In a two-person zero-sum game, the gain of one player is the loss of the other. The payoff matrix shows A's gains for every pair of *strategies* (A chooses a row, B a column). A strategy is a rule for choosing a course of action; a pure strategy uses one course of action with certainty. A plays to maximise and B to minimise A's payoff.
body.kn: ಆಟ ಎಂದರೆ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಹಿತಾಸಕ್ತಿಯ ಆಟಗಾರರ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಾತ್ಮಕ ಸನ್ನಿವೇಶ. ಇಬ್ಬರ ಶೂನ್ಯ-ಮೊತ್ತ ಆಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಬ್ಬರ ಲಾಭ ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬರ ನಷ್ಟ. ಪ್ರತಿಫಲ ಶ್ರೇಣಿ A ಯ ಲಾಭಗಳನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಶುದ್ಧ ತಂತ್ರ ಒಂದೇ ಕ್ರಮವನ್ನು ಖಚಿತವಾಗಿ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Here is the payoff matrix to player A. A chooses a row, B chooses a column.
A is cautious: for each row, write the worst case, the row minimum. The best of these, the maximin, is 4.
B is cautious too: for each column, write the column maximum. The smallest, the minimax, is 4.
Maximin equals minimax, so the game has a saddle point at A2, B2. The value of the game is 4.
Optimal strategies: A always plays A2 and B always plays B2. Neither can do better by changing alone.

say.en: A 3 times 3 payoff matrix gains of A. Each row minimum is listed on the right, each column maximum below. A picks the largest row minimum (maximin, yellow); B picks the smallest column maximum (minimax, blue). When they are equal, the green cell is a saddle point. Change three of the payoffs.

body.en: A selects the row whose minimum is largest: maximin value $\underline{v} = \max_i \min_j a_{ij}$. B selects the column whose maximum is smallest: minimax value $\overline{v} = \min_j \max_i a_{ij}$. Always $\underline{v} \le v \le \overline{v}$. If $\underline{v} = \overline{v}$, the game has a *saddle point*: the entry that is the minimum of its row and the maximum of its column. Its value is the value of the game $v$, and the game is strictly determinable. The game is fair if $v = 0$.
body.kn: A ಗರಿಷ್ಠ-ಕನಿಷ್ಠ (maximin), B ಕನಿಷ್ಠ-ಗರಿಷ್ಠ (minimax) ಆರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಎರಡೂ ಸಮಾನವಾದರೆ ಪಲ್ಲಣ ಬಿಂದು; ಅದರ ಬೆಲೆಯೇ ಆಟದ ಬೆಲೆ v. v = 0 ಆದರೆ ನ್ಯಾಯಯುತ ಆಟ.

points.en: *Saddle point*: least in its row, greatest in its column

narration.en: A selects the row whose minimum is largest: maximin value underlinev = max_i min_j a_ij. B selects the column whose maximum is smallest: minimax value overlinev = min_j max_i a_ij. Always underlinev ≤ v ≤ overlinev. If underlinev = overlinev, the game has a saddle point: the entry that is the minimum of its row and the maximum of its column. Its value is the value of the game v, and the game is strictly determinable. The game is fair if v = 0.
